subject: Segmentation expectations & POC next steps
messages:
From: Marco Silva <marco@luminahealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sana Rao <sana.rao@luminahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation needs follow-up from today

Hi Grace / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary from our side and the asks we want to make sure are captured before we move to a POC: 

- Data sensitivity: Lumina processes PHI and some highly regulated patient-identifying datasets. We need guarantees around logical separation and zero cross-tenant access.
- Preferred deployment: our compliance team strongly prefers a private control plane (VPC) for the pilot. That said, we asked whether Redwood Dedicated + customer-managed KMS would be acceptable as an interim option — please confirm the differences we should share with legal.
- Egress & auditability: must have TLS-in-transit assurances, no outbound data sharing beyond our project, and audit logs retained for 12 months.
- Network setup: we will likely require VPN or Direct Connect options and the ability to peer into our VPC.

Attachments: security_questionnaire.pdf (filled by our security team).

Next steps from our side: can you provide a short technical one-pager that states the guarantees for Dedicated vs Private (control plane residency, KMS ownership, audit log access), and a ballpark cost/time estimate for a 3-month POC? Ideally we’d get that before our legal review next Monday.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up if helpful.

Marco Silva
Director of Engineering, Lumina Health
marco@luminahealth.com
+1 415-555-0189

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation needs follow-up from today

Hi Marco / Sana —

Appreciate the clear summary and the questionnaire. Short recap and what I can commit to this week: 

Recap (Dedicated vs Private):
- Dedicated capacity: provides dedicated GPU pools and tenant-level data separation at the runtime layer. Control plane is still hosted (multi-tenant) unless you move to Private. With Dedicated you can use customer-managed KMS for model keys and artifacts, and we can provide access to tokenized audit logs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): provides a private control plane option where control plane components and telemetry can be placed into a customer VPC or on-prem bundle. Offers the strongest isolation guarantees for compliance-driven customers because admin and metadata surfaces are under your network boundaries.

I'll put together a concise one-pager that enumerates where data and metadata live in both modes, KMS options, and what audit/log access looks like. I can also include a simple network diagram and the minimal list of required network ports. Expect that by Friday EOD.

Questions for you (to tailor the POC):
- Is BYOK mandatory or would Lumina accept Redwood-managed keys with an attestation while we run the initial POC?
- Do you have an existing Direct Connect / VPN provider preference? If so, which cloud region will the peering terminate in?
- For audit retention: you noted 12 months — do you need raw KV cache traces or just request/response-level logs and metadata?

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send the one-pager + architecture stub by Friday.
2) Schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with Ben (SE) and your infra lead — do mornings PT work on Monday/Tuesday next week?
3) Share a mutual action plan template and a rough POC statement of work (timeline + milestones).

Ben will attach a short architecture drawing below that clarifies Dedicated vs Private in terms of control-plane residency.

Best,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable.

Quick technical note — adding this before Grace's one-pager lands so you have a short reference: 

- Dedicated: runtime & model-serving resources are dedicated to Lumina. Control plane components (deployments, rollout APIs, user management) remain in Redwood's hosted control plane unless you opt for Private. With Dedicated we can enable customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for model artifacts and keys; network peering (VPN/Direct Connect) is supported for data plane egress. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 with the retention you specify (we can configure 12 months).

- Private (VPC): we can deploy the control plane into a customer VPC (private control plane), including the admin UI endpoints and telemetry ingestion. That makes metadata and admin APIs subject to your network controls and firewalling. For on-prem bundles, we offer an air-gapped deployment package but that requires a longer lead time and a separate professional services SOW.

- Operational trade-offs: Dedicated = faster onboarding (weeks), Private VPC = more setup time (4–8 weeks depending on connectivity and approvals) but highest compliance posture.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-architecture.png (simple diagram). Will follow up in the deep-dive with configuration examples (firewall rules, sample IAM roles).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example.com

Grace / Ben —

Thanks for the clear, fast responses — that was helpful. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Control plane residency: Lumina's compliance team is going to ask for the private control plane for the POC. We understand Dedicated is an acceptable interim technical solution but it will require stronger attestations for metadata residency; legal will push back on hosted control planes.
- Timeline: we need the POC to start in July. Can Redwood commit to a 4–6 week prep window for a VPC-based control plane, assuming we approve the SOW this week? 
- Cost/ballpark: please include a short line item for the delta between Dedicated and Private for a 3-month POC (licensing delta + estimated infra).

I've attached a draft MOU (MOU_draft.docx) that our legal team started. Can you review and flag any items that are a hard stop for Redwood? Also please share the one-pager and architecture diagram when they are ready.

If you can get a mutual action plan/MAP + SOW + MOU comments by next Wednesday, we can aim to sign by the end of the month.

Marco Silva
Director of Engineering, Lumina Health
marco@luminahealth.com
+1 415-555-0189
